name: Belize Barrier Reef Reserve System
blurb: Reef, seagrass and mangrove: conch, turtles, groupers and sharks.

tip.title: Lose the parrotfish
tip.text: Parrotfish graze reef algae and feed groupers, sharks and dolphins. Set Stoplight parrotfish to -100% and watch the algae and the predators that eat them.

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage: Belize Barrier Reef Reserve System

notes: The story and why it matters come from the Wikipedia articles listed below (Belize Barrier Reef, Aliger gigas, Nassau grouper). Individual species and links have not been checked one by one. Feeding links that match a GloBI (Global Biotic Interactions) record are marked in the node details, with a link to the records. A few links were added from GloBI records.

nodes.desc: Microscopic drifting algae in the clear reef waters. They are the base of the plankton food chain.
Seagrass that carpets the sandy lagoon floor behind the reef. Conch, green turtles and manatees graze it.
Mangroves fringe the cayes and shoreline. Their leaves are eaten by manatees and their roots shelter young fish.

nodes.name: Copepods
nodes.desc: Tiny crustaceans of the plankton that graze phytoplankton and feed corals and many small animals.
Large sea snail that grazes algae and seagrass on sandy lagoon floors. It is food for turtles, lobsters, rays and nurse sharks.
Scrapes algae from reef rock with its beak-like teeth and excretes sand. Its grazing helps corals compete with algae.
Adults graze seagrass and algae. The reserve system protects nesting and feeding areas for green, hawksbill and loggerhead turtles.
Large herbivore of shallow coastal waters that eats seagrass and mangrove leaves. Boat strikes are a growing risk.
Night-feeding crustacean of reef crevices that eats snails such as conch, other molluscs and small animals.
Wide-ranging shark with a very broad diet that includes sea turtles and other sharks.

nodes.name: Common bottlenose dolphin
nodes.desc: Hunts fish in lagoons and along the reef, sometimes herding shoals. Large sharks are its main predators.
Clear shallow water lets light reach the seagrass, algae and coral on the sea floor.

nodes.name: Bacteria
nodes.desc: Break down dead plants and animals and return nutrients to the water and sediment.

story: The Belize Barrier Reef is a 300-kilometre section of the 900-kilometre Mesoamerican Barrier Reef System, the second largest coral reef system in the world. It includes three atolls and the Great Blue Hole at Lighthouse Reef. Darwin called it "the most remarkable reef in the West Indies."
matters: It has 70 hard coral species, 36 soft coral species and 500 fish species. About 90% of the reef still needs researching, so an estimated 10% of its species have been discovered.
